page.layout: Running head at top, with the page number at top left. Below it, two circular medallion portraits side by side, each with its inscription in the ring: left Lecapenus, right Romanus junior. Below them one text block of two paragraphs in one column. No notes in the margins, and no printed block under the text.

main_text.l: LECAPENVS ROMANVS
IVNIOR ROMANVS LEO
ROMANVS Lecapenus obscuro genere natus, insidias
Constantino parauit, imperiique Constantinopolitani socius
ac particeps ab eodem necessario adscitus est eodem quo
regnare coepit Constantinus anno, uti supra videre est: Helenam-
que Constantini filiam, pulsa matre Zoë uxorem habuit. Nec
tamen iusiurandum sanctissimum quod praestiterat Lecapenus
nec gener Constantinus obstitit, quo minus imperium & sibi
& Christophoro filio idem Lecapenus assereret. Cum autem
aduersus Bulgaros, Simeonémque eorum ducem, infeliciter
congressus esset, à Stephano & Constantino, filiis suis captus,
imperio exuitur, & in vicinam insulam in monasterium ad Phi-
losophandum relegatur. At cum iidem ipsi aduersus Constan-
tinum Leonis filium idem molirentur, in laqueum quem teten-
derant incidunt, nam & ipsimet, Lecapeni inquam filij, mona-
sterio mancipantur. Imperauit Romanus Lecapenus annos
ROMANVS Constantini, Leonis filij, filius iunior, post
patrem imperium suscepit Constantinopolitanum, quod
tamen alieno rexit arbitrio, nempe Nicephori Phocæ, de quo sta-
tim meminerimus, ubi & annorum supputationem inferam,
non hic ne bis id faciam. Fuit Romanus hic foris aduersus Sara-
cenos Cretam occupantes, & Turcas Asiam vastantes,
Nicephori ductu felix: domi in matrem ac sorores impius, ut regia
eiectæ, ob mærorem quòd regio essent exutæ vestitu, quæstum
fecerint meretricium: ipse ludis ac crapulæ deditus, anno im-
perij decimo, veneno potionatur. Vide ut supra.

marginalia.note: 39. Vide Liuthprandum lib.5.ca.9.10. & 11. Egna.lib.2. Cosmog. Munst. lib.4.

page.notes: The two medallions are woodcut portraits of Romanus Lecapenus (left, bearded, laureate, facing right) and Romanus junior (right, youthful, laureate, facing right); they are not transcribed as text. The marginal note "39. Vide..." stands in the left margin beside the words "annos" and is placed there in the transcription. Long s has been written as s throughout. Words broken at line ends without a printed hyphen (Phi-losophandum, teten-derant, Sara-cenos) are written whole.
